statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a UAS receives a request from a UAC, the UAS MAY authenticate the originator before the request is processed.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The WWW-Authenticate response-header field MUST be included in 401 (Unauthorized) response messages.
actions: include WWW-Authenticate header field in 401 response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the originating UAC receives the 401 (Unauthorized), it SHOULD, if it is able, re-originate the request with the proper credentials.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Once authentication credentials have been supplied (either directly by the user, or discovered in an internal keyring), UAs SHOULD cache the credentials for a given value of the To header field and "realm" and attempt to re-use these values on the next request for that destination.
actions: cache credentials keyed by To header field value and realm
re-use cached credentials on next request to same destination

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: UAs MAY cache credentials in any way they would like.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If no credentials for a realm can be located, UACs MAY attempt to retry the request with a username of "anonymous" and no password (a password of "").
actions: retry request with username=anonymous and empty password

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Once credentials have been located, any UA that wishes to authenticate itself with a UAS or registrar -- usually, but not necessarily, after receiving a 401 (Unauthorized) response -- MAY do so by including an Authorization header field with the request.
actions: include Authorization header field in outgoing request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a UAC resubmits a request with its credentials after receiving a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response, it MUST increment the CSeq header field value as it would normally when sending an updated request.
actions: increment CSeq header field value before resubmitting request
